topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the core learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional modalities of cancer treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic drivers and kinase signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapies targeting activated oncogenes and kinase pathways, along with the molecular mechanisms of inhibitor resistance and strategies to manage it.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the design and clinical mechanisms of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates targeted against cell surface proteins.

topics.label: Tumour immunology and cellular immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles of natural immune surveillance and immunotherapeutic modalities that harness or re-engineer T cells to eliminate tumour cells.

topics.label: Systemic challenges, trends, and future paradigms in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review overarching challenges, mortality trends, emerging paradigms, and clinical dilemmas shaping the future of cancer treatment.
